 JUDGMENT M.F.A. NO.1070 OF 2017 :
1.
The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.2,24,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the liability of the insurer to satisfy the accident is not in dispute.

3. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries :
 i. Lacerated left ankle  ii. Abrasion left shaft
iii . Fracture left thigh bone (femur)

4. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation:

5. The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8 % to the whole body.
The Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 8% despite the fact that the Doctor who treated the claimant stated that the claimant had suffered 17% disability to the whole body.
In my view, in the face of the clear evidence the Tribunal ought not to have reduced the disability.
It is, therefore, held that the claimant had suffered disability at 17% to the whole body.
6. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.7,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2015,
would be Rs.9,000/-.
7.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.3,30,480/- (Rs.9,000/-
x 12 x 18 x 17 %) towards 'loss of future income' .

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- towards conveyance, food, nutrition and incident expenses.
